chunks: Al-Shaykh, may Allah have mercy on him, informed me from Abu al-Qasim Ja'far ibn Muhammad, from his father, from Sa'd ibn 'Abd Allah, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, from 'Abd Allah ibn Sinan, who said:

My father asked Abu 'Abd Allah عليه السلام while I was present: I lend my garment to a dhimmi, and I know that he drinks wine and eats the flesh of swine. Then he returns it to me, so should I wash it before I perform salat in it?

So Abu 'Abd Allah عليه السلام said: Perform salat in it, and do not wash it on account of that, for you lent it to him while it was tahir, and you have not become certain that he made it najis. So there is no problem in performing salat in it until you become certain that he made it najis.

key_terms.الذِّمِّيَّ: a non-Muslim living under Muslim protection
key_terms.الْخَمْرَ: wine or intoxicating drink, mentioned here as a najis-related concern
key_terms.تَسْتَيْقِنَ: to attain certainty, as opposed to mere doubt
key_terms.لَحْمَ الْخِنْزِيرِ: swine flesh, mentioned as a source associated with najasah

ai.seo_question: Can you pray in clothes returned by a non-Muslim who drinks wine and eats pork?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling regarding a garment lent to a dhimmi who is known to drink wine and eat pork. Imam al-Sadiq عليه السلام states that the garment remains tahir and may be used for salat unless there is certainty that it has become najis, establishing that mere suspicion does not remove the presumption of purity.
